description: A background process a shell step starts (a detached grandchild left in the step's own process group, the way a real shell step's own `foo &` backgrounds something -- see this case's own `fakes/fake`) survives the step finishing normally -- only the step's own process group would make it exit, and normal completion must not kill that group (#519). `start` writes the grandchild's pid to a pidfile rather than echoing it as a step value (a fresh pid every run, which `expected.json` can't commit to); `check` reads it to confirm the grandchild is still alive right after `start` returns, never via a process-name search; `cleanup` kills it by pid and removes the pidfile, so the case leaves nothing behind.
